headline: High: shared filesystem and clipboard/screen surfaces make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; AutoGPT’s shell access raises conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while ChatGPT Desktop can ingest user-uploaded files, clipboard, screenshots, and app context. That creates a plausible bridge where malicious content from one can influence the other without a dedicated provenance layer. The pathway is not proven by docs, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the pair exchanges content through shared files, clipboard, or screenshots
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats imported content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use separate folders for each agent's files
Add a manual review step before either agent executes instructions from the other
Strip prompts from screenshots and pasted text before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and shell execution. If they share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive material can flow from B into A outputs or vice versa. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets handling, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or copied artifacts
IF uploaded files or IDE code are reused in AutoGPT prompts or outputs
mitigations: Keep each agent in a separate workspace
Avoid pasting sensitive files into shared chats
Turn off or limit file sharing for one agent during the other’s run
Review outputs before forwarding them across agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files from supported macOS apps and use vendor-mediated tools. Even though B cannot write files or modify git state, overlapping access to the same local resources can still cause racey edits or inconsistent reads if both operate on shared inputs. The lack of explicit locking keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local project tree
IF AutoGPT writes or mutates files while ChatGPT Desktop reads app-context copies of those files
mitigations: Run the agents on separate copies of the project
Pause one agent while the other is mutating files
Use read-only mounts for ChatGPT Desktop inputs
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repository
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can consume files, screenshots, and app context, so it may treat AutoGPT-generated artifacts as authoritative inputs. AutoGPT can also generate shell-driven outputs that B may summarize or act on. Because the pair lacks a documented verification boundary and B has downstream tool access, a mistaken AutoGPT output can cascade into incorrect actions or reports.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop forwards AutoGPT output into a tool action or user-facing summary
IF AutoGPT-produced text is accepted without independent verification
mitigations: Require human verification before any action based on AutoGPT output
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite source files before acting
Use a checklist to verify key facts from independent sources
Limit AutoGPT to draft-only mode for sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop explicitly touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access. If regulated data is placed into those surfaces, the pair can create a residency or retention mismatch because B is vendor-mediated and A’s storage/handling is unspecified. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into ChatGPT Desktop or AutoGPT workspaces
IF the deployment requires a specific residency, retention, or DPA guarantee not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair's shared workflow
Use synthetic or redacted inputs for testing
Check vendor retention settings before use
Document which data classes each agent may touch
requires-engineering: obtain a formal compliance review for the deployment
